questionText: Which international organization sets widely accepted rules for international trade terms used in foreign procurement?
options: World Bank
International Chamber of Commerce (ICC)
United Nations Development Programme
World Trade Organization

questionText: What does the term "Incoterms" refer to in foreign procurement?
options: International tax regulations for cross-border trade
A set of internationally recognized rules defining responsibilities of buyers and sellers in trade
Currency exchange standards for international payments
Customs clearance procedures for imported goods

questionText: A company in Ethiopia wants to import machinery from Germany. Under CIF terms, who is responsible for freight and insurance costs?
options: The buyer (Ethiopian company)
The seller (German company)
The freight forwarder
The customs authority

questionText: Which of the following is a key difference between domestic and foreign procurement?
options: Foreign procurement never requires competitive bidding
Foreign procurement involves additional complexities such as currency risk, customs procedures, and international regulations
Domestic procurement always takes longer than foreign procurement
Foreign procurement is exclusively managed by the Ministry of Finance

questionText: What does "FOB" stand for in international trade terms?
options: Freight on Board
Free on Board
Forward Order Bid
Final Order Billing

questionText: Under FOB terms, when does the risk of loss transfer from the seller to the buyer?
options: When the goods are loaded onto the vessel at the port of shipment
When the goods arrive at the buyer's warehouse
When the buyer pays the invoice
When the customs authority clears the goods

questionText: Which of the following documents is most critical for customs clearance of imported goods?
options: The procurement plan
The commercial invoice and bill of lading
The bid evaluation report
The letter of credit application form

questionText: What is the primary purpose of a letter of credit (LC) in foreign procurement?
options: To insure goods during international transportation
To guarantee payment to the seller upon presentation of compliant shipping documents
To register the buyer with the customs authority
To provide a framework for dispute resolution between buyer and seller

questionText: Which of the following best describes "international competitive bidding" (ICB)?
options: A method reserved exclusively for procurement of consulting services
A procurement method where qualified suppliers from any country can submit bids
A procurement method limited to suppliers within the African continent
A procurement method used only for emergency situations

questionText: What is a pro forma invoice in foreign procurement?
options: The final invoice issued after goods are delivered
A preliminary document issued by the seller showing estimated price, terms, and conditions before the actual transaction
A customs declaration form submitted by the buyer
A bank document guaranteeing payment to the seller

questionText: Which Incoterm requires the seller to bear all costs and risks until the goods are delivered to the buyer's named destination?
options: FOB
EXW
DDP (Delivered Duty Paid)
CFR

questionText: What is the main function of a freight forwarder in international procurement?
options: To manufacture goods for export
To organize and coordinate the shipment of goods on behalf of the buyer or seller
To issue letters of credit on behalf of the buyer's bank
To inspect goods at the seller's warehouse

questionText: Which of the following is a common risk associated with foreign procurement?
options: Excessive number of domestic suppliers
Currency fluctuation, longer lead times, and complex customs procedures
Over-transparency in the bidding process
Too many competitive suppliers in the local market

questionText: What is the purpose of a packing list in an international shipment?
options: To confirm that payment has been made to the seller
To detail the contents, weight, and dimensions of each package in the shipment
To serve as the primary customs clearance document
To specify the Incoterm applicable to the shipment

questionText: Under which Incoterm does the buyer bear maximum responsibility from the point of origin?
options: DDP
CIF
EXW (Ex Works)
DAP

questionText: What is a bill of lading (B/L) in international trade?
options: A contract between the buyer and the customs authority
A transport document issued by the carrier acknowledging receipt of goods for shipment
A form submitted to the bank to initiate payment
A certificate confirming the quality of exported goods

questionText: Which of the following is a key element of a tender document for foreign procurement?
options: The personal financial details of procurement officers
Technical specifications, commercial terms, eligibility criteria, and evaluation methodology
The names of all expected foreign suppliers
The internal budget ceiling of the procuring entity

questionText: What is the role of a certificate of origin in international trade?
options: To confirm the seller's bank account details for payment
To certify the country in which the goods were manufactured, which may affect tariffs and trade agreements
To authorize customs clearance in the destination country
To confirm that goods have been inspected and meet quality standards

questionText: Which of the following best explains "currency risk" in foreign procurement?
options: The risk of receiving counterfeit currency from a foreign supplier
The risk that exchange rate fluctuations will increase the effective cost of imported goods
The risk of being charged additional taxes by a foreign government
The risk that the supplier will demand payment in a non-convertible currency

questionText: What does "insurance certificate" in an international shipment confirm?
options: That the goods have cleared customs in the destination country
That the goods are insured against loss or damage during transit
That the seller has paid all applicable export duties
That the buyer has received and inspected the goods

questionText: Which of the following is a common method of payment in international procurement besides letters of credit?
options: Barter trade agreements
Documentary collection (D/C)
Advance customs payment
Freight insurance payment

questionText: What is the significance of Incoterms in a foreign procurement contract?
options: They set the legal jurisdiction for dispute resolution
They define the point at which risk and cost transfer from seller to buyer
They determine the applicable tariff rate for imported goods
They specify the quality standards the goods must meet

questionText: A procurement officer is evaluating a foreign bid with prices in USD. The evaluation must be done in ETB. What factor must be applied?
options: The price should be accepted as-is without conversion
The applicable exchange rate on the bid closing date or as specified in the bidding documents
The seller's preferred exchange rate
The exchange rate on the date of contract signing

questionText: Which of the following documents is required to open a letter of credit at a bank?
options: The procurement plan approved by the head of the organization
The pro forma invoice, import permit, and bank application form
The bid evaluation report and contract award letter
The customs declaration form and packing list

questionText: What is the purpose of an import permit in foreign procurement?
options: To authorize the seller to export goods from their country
To authorize the buyer to bring specific goods into the country in compliance with national regulations
To confirm that the buyer has paid the full purchase price
To replace the letter of credit in simple trade transactions

questionText: Which of the following international shipping terms requires the seller to deliver goods at a named terminal at the destination, unloaded?
options: FOB
DAT (Delivered at Terminal)
EXW
CFR

questionText: What is the role of a pre-shipment inspection in international procurement?
options: To inspect goods after they arrive at the buyer's warehouse
To verify the quality, quantity, and compliance of goods before they are shipped
To confirm that customs duties have been paid by the seller
To evaluate the financial capacity of the foreign supplier

questionText: Which of the following is a key challenge in preparing tender documents for foreign procurement?
options: Excessive number of domestic suppliers bidding on international tenders
Addressing international standards, currency considerations, language barriers, and compliance with multiple legal systems
Limiting participation to suppliers from a single country
Avoiding the use of Incoterms in contract documentation

questionText: What does "CIF" stand for in Incoterms?
options: Contract, Insurance, and Freight
Cost, Insurance, and Freight
Customs, Inspection, and Forwarding
Carriage, Insurance, and Final delivery

questionText: Under CIF terms, which costs are included in the seller's price?
options: Import duties and customs clearance at destination
Cost of goods, marine insurance, and freight to the destination port
Unloading costs at destination and inland delivery
All costs until goods are delivered to the buyer's warehouse

questionText: Which of the following is a key criterion for evaluating foreign bids?
options: The nationality of the supplier's management team
Technical compliance, evaluated price, and delivery terms
The geographic location of the supplier's headquarters
The number of countries where the supplier has previously operated

questionText: What is "country of origin" preference in procurement evaluation?
options: Awarding contracts only to suppliers in the buyer's country
A price adjustment applied during bid evaluation to give domestic suppliers a comparative advantage
A rule requiring all foreign suppliers to establish local offices before bidding
A policy that exempts domestic goods from import taxes

questionText: Which of the following best describes a "back-to-back letter of credit"?
options: An LC issued by the seller's bank to guarantee payment to the buyer
A secondary LC opened by the intermediary trader in favor of the actual supplier, backed by the original LC
An LC used exclusively for domestic procurement transactions
A guarantee issued by the buyer's government to the seller's bank

questionText: What is the purpose of a "performance bond" in a foreign procurement contract?
options: To guarantee that the buyer will pay the seller on time
To protect the buyer if the foreign supplier fails to fulfill contractual obligations
To confirm that the supplier has cleared customs in the buyer's country
To replace the letter of credit in long-term supply contracts

questionText: Which of the following is a common eligibility criterion for participating in international competitive bidding?
options: The supplier must be a citizen of the buyer's country
The supplier must have relevant technical experience, financial capacity, and not be debarred
The supplier must have previously supplied goods to the buyer's government
The supplier must be registered in the buyer's country before submitting a bid

questionText: What is a "sight letter of credit"?
options: An LC payable 90 days after the goods are shipped
An LC that requires the bank to pay immediately upon presentation of compliant documents
An LC used exclusively for construction contract payments
An LC that does not require presentation of shipping documents

questionText: Which of the following factors is most important when selecting an Incoterm for a foreign procurement contract?
options: The personal preference of the procurement officer
The agreed allocation of risk, cost, and responsibility between buyer and seller
The currency in which the contract is denominated
The number of ports available in the seller's country

questionText: What is the significance of the "Harmonized System (HS) Code" in international trade?
options: It sets the exchange rate for international procurement transactions
It provides a standardized numerical code for classifying traded goods, used by customs authorities worldwide
It specifies the Incoterm applicable to each category of goods
It determines the insurance premium for each shipment

questionText: Which of the following is a key document in the letter of credit process?
options: The supplier's company registration certificate
The bill of lading, commercial invoice, and certificate of origin
The procurement plan of the buying organization
The bank guarantee issued by the buyer's government

questionText: What is the primary purpose of a "tender bond" (bid security) in international procurement?
options: To cover transportation costs if goods are damaged during shipment
To ensure that the bidder will not withdraw their bid or refuse to sign the contract if selected
To guarantee that the buyer will pay the full contract amount
To cover the cost of bid evaluation in international tendering

questionText: Under which Incoterm does the seller bear the maximum responsibility including import duties at the destination?
options: FOB
CIF
EXW
DDP

questionText: Which of the following best describes "open account" as a payment method in foreign procurement?
options: The seller ships goods and receives payment before shipment
The seller ships goods and extends credit to the buyer, who pays after a specified period
The buyer pays through a bank-guaranteed letter of credit
Payment is made through a third-party escrow account

questionText: What is the main purpose of a "warranty" clause in a foreign procurement contract?
options: To specify the Incoterm applicable to the delivery
To obligate the foreign supplier to repair or replace defective goods within a specified period after delivery
To set the exchange rate for payments made after delivery
To specify the port of loading for the shipment

questionText: Which of the following is a benefit of international competitive bidding over domestic procurement?
options: It simplifies customs clearance procedures
It expands the pool of suppliers, potentially improving quality and reducing costs
It eliminates the need for technical specifications
It reduces the time required to complete the procurement process

questionText: What is the role of SWIFT in international payment transactions?
options: To insure international shipments against loss or damage
To provide a secure messaging network for international financial transactions between banks
To classify traded goods using the Harmonized System codes
To issue letters of credit on behalf of importing countries

questionText: Which of the following best explains why foreign procurement typically has longer lead times than domestic procurement?
options: Foreign suppliers always charge higher prices than domestic suppliers
International shipping, customs clearance, and compliance with multiple regulatory requirements add time to the process
Foreign suppliers require more detailed technical specifications
International competitive bidding requires more bidders than domestic procurement

questionText: What is the significance of "Incoterms 2020" in foreign procurement?
options: They replaced all previous trade terms with a completely new set of rules
They are the most current version of international trade terms published by the ICC, updating and clarifying obligations of buyers and sellers
They apply exclusively to air freight transactions
They are mandatory under Ethiopian law for all foreign procurement contracts

questionText: What does "DAP" (Delivered at Place) mean in Incoterms?
options: The seller pays for delivery to a named port and the buyer handles all remaining costs
The seller is responsible for delivering goods to a named place at destination, with the buyer responsible for unloading and import duties
The buyer pays for all costs from the point of origin to the destination

questionText: Which of the following is a key risk management strategy in foreign procurement?
options: Avoiding the use of Incoterms to maintain flexibility
Using forward exchange contracts to hedge against currency fluctuation risks
Limiting foreign procurement to a single trusted supplier
Paying suppliers before goods are shipped to ensure priority service

questionText: What is the purpose of a "draft" in documentary collection as a payment method?
options: To specify the quality standards of the goods being purchased
A financial instrument ordering the buyer's bank to pay a specific amount at a specified time
A preliminary version of the letter of credit
A customs declaration form submitted by the importer

questionText: Which of the following international standards is commonly referenced in technical specifications for foreign procurement?
options: Standards set by the local chamber of commerce
ISO (International Organization for Standardization) standards
Standards developed by the buyer's procurement unit
Standards established by the seller's national government

questionText: What is the key advantage of using CIF over FOB for an Ethiopian importer?
options: The Ethiopian importer bears less risk since the seller arranges insurance and freight
CIF is always cheaper than FOB for Ethiopian importers
CIF eliminates the need for customs clearance
CIF does not require a letter of credit

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a non-tariff barrier that can affect foreign procurement?
options: Import duties applied to all goods
Technical standards, labeling requirements, or import quotas that restrict market access
Exchange rate fluctuations in the international market
Competition from domestic suppliers

questionText: What is a "standby letter of credit" in foreign trade?
options: A type of letter of credit used exclusively for air freight
A backup payment guarantee that is drawn upon only if the buyer fails to fulfill payment obligations
A letter of credit that expires if not used within 30 days
A credit facility issued by the buyer's government for emergency imports

questionText: Which document provides the buyer with evidence of title to goods in international trade?
options: The certificate of origin
The negotiable bill of lading
The commercial invoice
The insurance certificate

questionText: Under Ethiopian foreign procurement rules, which government body is typically responsible for approving import permits?
options: The Ministry of Education
The Ethiopian Trade and Industry Ministry or relevant sector authority
The Public Procurement and Property Administration Agency
The National Bank of Ethiopia exclusively

questionText: What is "demurrage" in international shipping?
options: A fee charged by the seller for late payment
A charge imposed on the buyer for keeping a container beyond the agreed free period
A customs penalty for misdeclared goods
A freight discount offered for bulk shipments

questionText: Which of the following is a key responsibility of the buyer under EXW (Ex Works) terms?
options: The buyer only pays for unloading at the destination
The buyer bears all costs and risks from the seller's premises to the final destination

questionText: What is the purpose of a "certificate of conformity" in international procurement?
options: To confirm that the buyer has paid for the goods
To certify that the goods meet the specified technical standards or contractual requirements
To authorize customs clearance of goods at the destination port
To guarantee payment to the seller through the banking system

questionText: Which of the following is a key factor in determining the most appropriate Incoterm for a foreign procurement contract?
options: The language used in the tender document
The mode of transport, value of goods, and the buyer's capacity to manage logistics
The number of ports available in the seller's country
The currency in which the contract is denominated

questionText: What is the purpose of the "bid evaluation criteria" in international competitive bidding?
options: To determine the exchange rate applicable to the contract
To provide a transparent and consistent basis for comparing and selecting the best bid
To limit participation to pre-qualified foreign suppliers

questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of a well-prepared international tender document?
options: It contains vague technical specifications to allow maximum supplier flexibility
It provides clear, complete, and unambiguous information enabling fair competition
It restricts participation to suppliers from specific countries

questionText: What is the role of the National Bank of Ethiopia in foreign procurement transactions?
options: To evaluate bids from foreign suppliers
To regulate foreign exchange transactions and approve the opening of letters of credit
To prepare tender documents for international procurement
To grant import permits for restricted goods

questionText: Which of the following is the correct definition of "counterfeit goods" in the context of foreign procurement?
options: Goods that are more expensive than originally quoted
Goods that are fraudulently branded or falsely represented as meeting specified standards

questionText: What is the purpose of a "shipping guarantee" in international trade?
options: To ensure that goods are insured during transit
To allow the buyer to take delivery of goods before the original bill of lading arrives
To guarantee that the seller ships on the agreed date

questionText: Which of the following best explains why pre-shipment inspection is important in foreign procurement?
options: It eliminates the need for customs clearance at destination
It verifies that goods comply with contractual specifications before leaving the seller's country, reducing the risk of receiving defective or substandard goods

questionText: What is a "force majeure" clause in a foreign procurement contract?
options: A clause that allows the buyer to cancel the contract at any time
A clause that excuses both parties from contractual obligations due to extraordinary events beyond their control

questionText: Which of the following is a key advantage of documentary credit (letter of credit) over open account payment?
options: It is cheaper and faster than open account
It provides greater payment security for the seller and document verification for the buyer
It eliminates the need for shipping documents
It allows the buyer to negotiate prices after shipment

questionText: What is the primary purpose of the "advance payment guarantee" in foreign procurement?
options: To guarantee that the buyer will pay the full contract amount at contract signing
To protect the buyer if the supplier fails to repay the advance in the event of non-performance

questionText: Which of the following is a key risk associated with single-source foreign procurement?
options: Excessive competition from domestic suppliers
Lack of competition, potential for overpricing, and dependency on a single foreign supplier
Longer customs clearance procedures for competitive bids
Difficulty in preparing technical specifications for foreign goods

questionText: Under which Incoterm is the seller responsible for delivering goods cleared for import, with all duties paid, at the named destination?
options: FOB
DAP
CIF
DDP

questionText: What is a "usance letter of credit"?
options: An LC payable immediately upon presentation of documents
An LC that allows the buyer a deferred payment period after presentation of compliant documents
An LC issued exclusively for emergency procurement
An LC that does not require a bill of lading

questionText: Which of the following is a key consideration when drafting technical specifications for foreign procurement?
options: Limiting specifications to brands available only from a single country
Ensuring specifications are based on international standards and functional requirements to encourage maximum competition
Including detailed instructions on how suppliers should manufacture the goods

questionText: What does "transit time" refer to in foreign procurement planning?
options: The time taken to evaluate bids in international competitive bidding
The time required for goods to travel from the seller's location to the buyer's destination
The time allowed for the buyer to inspect goods after delivery

questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of using a freight forwarder in foreign procurement?
options: Freight forwarders guarantee the lowest possible shipping rates at all times
Freight forwarders manage complex logistics, documentation, and customs procedures on behalf of the buyer
Freight forwarders eliminate the need for letters of credit

questionText: What is the main purpose of "trade finance" in the context of foreign procurement?
options: To provide training for procurement officers on international trade rules
To provide financial instruments and products that facilitate international trade by reducing payment risk
To set exchange rates for international transactions
To regulate import duties and tariffs on traded goods

questionText: Which of the following best describes "import substitution" as a procurement policy?
options: Replacing foreign procurement officers with domestic staff
A policy that encourages domestic production to reduce dependence on imported goods
Substituting cheaper foreign goods for more expensive domestic equivalents
A practice of replacing one foreign supplier with another during contract execution

questionText: What is the role of the "confirming bank" in a letter of credit transaction?
options: To issue the original letter of credit on behalf of the buyer
To add its own guarantee to the LC, assuring the seller of payment even if the issuing bank defaults
To inspect goods before shipment on behalf of the buyer

questionText: Which of the following is a key benefit of harmonizing procurement procedures with international standards such as those of the World Bank?
options: It eliminates the need for domestic procurement regulations
It facilitates access to international financing, improves transparency, and attracts more competitive bids

questionText: What is the significance of the "validity period" of a bid in international competitive bidding?

It is the period during which the bidder's offer remains binding and the procuring entity must complete evaluation and award

questionText: Which of the following is a primary function of the "advising bank" in a letter of credit transaction?
options: To guarantee payment to the seller if the issuing bank fails
To notify the seller that an LC has been issued in their favor
To inspect goods before they are shipped to the buyer

questionText: What is the purpose of a "discrepancy notice" in a letter of credit transaction?
options: To inform the buyer that the seller has shipped the wrong goods
To notify the seller that their documents do not comply with LC terms and may not be honored
To cancel the letter of credit before the expiry date

questionText: Which of the following is a key principle that should guide foreign procurement decisions?
options: Always select the supplier with the lowest price regardless of quality
Balance quality, cost, delivery, and risk to achieve value for money
Prioritize suppliers from countries with which Ethiopia has diplomatic ties

questionText: What is the purpose of a "black clause" or "on deck" notation on a bill of lading?

To notify the buyer that goods are stowed on deck, which may affect the risk profile and insurance coverage
To confirm that all import duties have been prepaid by the seller

questionText: Which of the following is an obligation of the buyer under CIF terms?
options: Arranging and paying for freight to the destination port
Paying for unloading costs and import duties at the destination
Obtaining marine insurance for the goods during transit
Completing export customs formalities in the seller's country

questionText: What is the role of "Incoterms" in resolving trade disputes?
options: They serve as a binding legal framework that overrides national laws
They provide a common reference for interpreting the responsibilities of buyer and seller, reducing misunderstandings
They specify the jurisdiction where disputes must be resolved
They set the penalty for late delivery in international contracts

questionText: Which of the following is a key step in the process of opening a letter of credit?
options: The seller applies to their bank to issue the LC in favor of the buyer
The buyer applies to their bank to issue the LC in favor of the seller
The freight forwarder issues the LC after goods are shipped
The customs authority approves the LC before goods are cleared

questionText: What is the significance of "SWIFT codes" in international procurement payments?
options: They classify goods for customs and tariff purposes
They identify specific banks in the international payment network, enabling accurate routing of funds
They specify the Incoterm applicable to the transaction
They determine the insurance premium for international shipments

questionText: Which of the following best describes a "revolving letter of credit"?
options: An LC that can only be used once and expires after the first transaction
An LC that automatically renews for the same amount and period after each drawing, suitable for ongoing procurement
An LC that requires the buyer to pay before goods are shipped

questionText: What is the purpose of the "negotiating bank" in an LC transaction?
options: To issue the letter of credit on behalf of the buyer
To examine the seller's documents and advance funds against them before receiving payment from the issuing bank

questionText: Which of the following is a key factor to consider when evaluating the financial capacity of a foreign supplier?
options: The number of languages spoken by the supplier's management team
Financial statements, credit ratings, and ability to fulfill the contract value
The age of the company's founding documents
The number of countries where the supplier has received awards

questionText: What is the primary purpose of "trade credit insurance" in foreign procurement?
options: To insure goods against damage during international transportation
To protect the buyer against the risk of supplier default or non-delivery
To cover the cost of customs duties on imported goods
To guarantee the performance of the freight forwarder

questionText: Which of the following international arbitration forums is commonly specified for dispute resolution in foreign procurement contracts?
options: The World Trade Organization's dispute panel
The International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) International Court of Arbitration
The United Nations General Assembly
The World Bank Inspection Panel

questionText: What is the key advantage of using a framework agreement for recurring foreign procurement?
options: It eliminates the need for any future competitive bidding for listed items
It reduces repetitive tendering and speeds up procurement for regularly needed goods while maintaining agreed pricing
It guarantees the same price regardless of market fluctuations

questionText: Which of the following is a key difference between a "confirmed" and an "unconfirmed" letter of credit?

A confirmed LC carries the additional payment guarantee of a second bank in the seller's country, reducing the seller's risk

questionText: What is the significance of "UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration" in foreign procurement contracts?

questionText: Which of the following is a best practice when preparing a bid for an international tender?
options: Submitting the bid after the deadline to avoid early disqualification
Carefully reviewing all tender documents, ensuring full compliance and submitting all required documentation on time
Offering the lowest price to guarantee selection regardless of quality

questionText: What is the primary purpose of "trade terms" specified in a foreign procurement contract?
options: To set the warranty period for delivered goods
To define the point where risk and responsibility transfer between buyer and seller
To determine the applicable import tariff rate
To specify the payment currency

questionText: Which of the following is a key consideration when specifying delivery terms in a foreign procurement contract?
options: The procurement officer's personal preference for shipping mode
The buyer's logistics capacity, insurance arrangements, and cost-effectiveness of each option
The seller's preferred Incoterm regardless of the buyer's needs

questionText: What is the role of "transit insurance" in foreign procurement?
options: To cover the cost of customs duties on imported goods
To protect goods against loss, damage, or theft during international transportation
To guarantee payment to the seller if the buyer defaults
To replace the performance bond in foreign contracts

questionText: Which of the following is a key challenge when conducting tender evaluation for foreign procurement?

Currency conversion, assessment of international technical standards, and verification of foreign supplier credentials
Too many bidders submitting identical offers

To withhold a portion of the contract payment until the supplier fulfills all obligations, including warranty requirements

questionText: Which of the following is a benefit of conducting pre-bid conferences in international competitive bidding?

They give potential bidders the opportunity to seek clarifications, improving the quality of bids received

questionText: What is the meaning of "transferable letter of credit"?

An LC that allows the seller to transfer part or all of the credit to one or more secondary beneficiaries
An LC that expires and is re-issued automatically after each transaction

questionText: Which of the following is a key risk in using advance payment in foreign procurement?
options: The seller may delay shipment to negotiate a better price
The buyer may lose the advance if the supplier fails to deliver or becomes insolvent
The buyer may be required to pay additional customs duties
The seller may demand a letter of credit after receiving the advance

questionText: What is the purpose of a "certificate of insurance" in a CIF shipment?
options: To confirm that the buyer has paid the seller
To provide the buyer with evidence that the goods are insured against transit risks
To authorize the freight forwarder to release goods at the destination port
To confirm that goods have been inspected and meet quality standards

questionText: Which of the following best describes "competitive dialogue" as a procurement method in complex international procurement?
options: A method where bidders negotiate prices openly in a public forum
A method where the procuring entity conducts structured discussions with pre-qualified bidders to develop solutions before requesting final bids
A method where the lowest bid is automatically selected without evaluation
A method restricted to procurement of consulting services

questionText: What is the significance of the "expiry date" in a letter of credit?
options: It is the date by which the buyer must open the LC
It is the deadline by which the seller must present compliant documents to receive payment
It is the date by which goods must arrive at the destination port

questionText: Which of the following is a key difference between "documentary credit" and "documentary collection"?
options: Documentary credit is cheaper and faster than documentary collection
Documentary credit provides bank guarantee of payment while documentary collection relies on the buyer's willingness to pay upon document presentation
Documentary collection is used exclusively for air freight transactions
Documentary credit does not require the presentation of shipping documents

questionText: What is the purpose of specifying a "governing law" clause in a foreign procurement contract?
options: To specify which country's customs regulations apply

questionText: Which of the following is a key element of effective supplier management in foreign procurement?
options: Changing suppliers frequently to maintain competitive pricing
Building and maintaining relationships with reliable foreign suppliers through performance monitoring and communication
Limiting foreign procurement to a single country to simplify management
Avoiding long-term contracts to maintain maximum procurement flexibility

questionText: What is the role of "trade facilitation" measures in foreign procurement?
options: To restrict the number of foreign suppliers participating in tenders
To simplify and harmonize customs and border procedures, reducing the cost and time of cross-border trade
To set minimum prices for imported goods
To require foreign suppliers to establish local offices before bidding

questionText: Which of the following is the key purpose of "country risk assessment" in foreign procurement?
options: To determine the tariff rate applicable to goods from a specific country
To evaluate the political, economic, and regulatory risks associated with sourcing from a particular country
To set the exchange rate for contracts with suppliers from high-risk countries
To determine the appropriate Incoterm for each country

questionText: What is the significance of "most-favored-nation (MFN)" treatment in international trade relevant to procurement?
options: It gives preference to goods from developing countries
It requires that trade concessions granted to one country be extended equally to all other trading partners under WTO rules
It allows governments to exclude foreign suppliers from public tenders
It exempts government procurement from international trade rules

questionText: Which of the following is a key obligation of the importer under Ethiopian customs regulations?
options: Paying freight costs on behalf of the foreign supplier
Accurately declaring imported goods, paying applicable duties, and complying with all import regulations
Inspecting goods at the seller's warehouse before shipment
Issuing the bill of lading for international shipments

questionText: What is the purpose of a "duty drawback" scheme in international trade?
options: To increase import duties on competitive foreign goods
To refund customs duties paid on imported goods that are subsequently re-exported or used in the production of exported goods
To exempt all government imports from customs duties
To compensate domestic suppliers for price disadvantages in international competition

questionText: Which of the following is a key characteristic of international competitive bidding as recommended by multilateral development banks?
options: Contracts are awarded to domestic suppliers by default
Open, transparent, and competitive bidding with international participation and standardized evaluation criteria
Bids are evaluated using only price criteria without technical assessment
Pre-qualification is mandatory for all ICB contracts regardless of value

questionText: What is the purpose of "addenda" issued during the international bidding process?
options: To notify unsuccessful bidders of their disqualification
To communicate changes, corrections, or clarifications to all potential bidders before the bid submission deadline
To extend the warranty period of goods delivered under a previous contract
To request additional financial documents from shortlisted bidders

questionText: Which of the following best describes "parallel importing" in the context of foreign procurement?
options: Importing the same goods from two different countries simultaneously
Importing genuine goods through unauthorized distribution channels, often at lower prices than official channels
Using two freight forwarders for the same shipment to reduce risk
Procuring goods under both an LC and an open account simultaneously

questionText: What is the primary purpose of "harmonizing" procurement procedures with international standards?
options: To eliminate domestic procurement rules
To ensure compatibility with international best practices, facilitating access to international financing and reducing procurement costs
To mandate the use of foreign suppliers for all major procurement
To restrict participation in tenders to internationally certified companies

questionText: Which of the following is a key element of a bid evaluation report in international procurement?
options: The personal opinions of the procurement officer on each bidder
A systematic comparison of bids against predetermined criteria with documented scores and a justified recommendation
A list of all suppliers who expressed interest but did not submit bids
The internal budget ceiling used to assess bid prices

questionText: What is the significance of "country preference margins" in World Bank-financed procurement?
options: They exclude foreign suppliers from participating in domestic tenders
They allow domestic bidders a price advantage during evaluation to support local industry development
They set the maximum contract value for which domestic procurement is permitted
They determine the exchange rate used for bid evaluation

questionText: Which of the following is a key challenge of procuring from a foreign supplier with a poor track record?
options: Excessive competition from the supplier's domestic market
Risk of non-delivery, quality failures, delayed shipments, and difficulty in enforcing contract remedies across jurisdictions
High competition from other buyers seeking the same supplier
Over-documentation requirements by the supplier's government

questionText: What is the role of the "issuing bank" in a letter of credit transaction?
options: To transport goods on behalf of the buyer
To issue the LC at the buyer's request, committing to pay the seller upon presentation of compliant documents
To inspect goods before they are shipped
To advise the seller of the LC terms and conditions

questionText: Which of the following is a key reason why Ethiopia uses foreign procurement for certain goods?
options: Domestic goods are always of lower quality than foreign goods
Some goods are not produced locally, or foreign sources offer better quality, technology, or value for money
Foreign procurement is always cheaper than domestic procurement
Ethiopian law mandates the use of foreign suppliers for all government contracts

questionText: What is the purpose of a "quality assurance" clause in a foreign procurement contract?
options: To specify the payment terms applicable to the contract
To define quality standards and inspection procedures the supplier must follow to ensure goods meet specifications
To set the freight terms for international delivery
To determine the warranty period for delivered goods

questionText: Which of the following is a key benefit of consolidating foreign procurement needs across government agencies?
options: It eliminates the need for competitive bidding in international procurement
It achieves economies of scale, reduces procurement costs, and simplifies contract management
It allows each agency to negotiate directly with preferred suppliers
It limits foreign procurement to a single government ministry

questionText: What is the primary purpose of "cargo tracking" in foreign procurement?
options: To calculate the customs duty payable on imported goods
To monitor the movement of goods in transit and anticipate delivery, enabling proactive management of any delays
To ensure that the seller ships goods on the correct vessel
To verify the accuracy of the bill of lading

questionText: Which of the following is a key consideration in choosing between air freight and sea freight for foreign procurement?
options: The personal preference of the freight forwarder
The urgency of the requirement, cost, nature of goods, and volume to be shipped
The number of customs checkpoints between origin and destination
The availability of the goods at the seller's warehouse

questionText: What is the purpose of a "dispute resolution clause" in a foreign procurement contract?
options: To specify the currency in which disputes must be settled
To define the process and forum for resolving disagreements between buyer and seller
To set the maximum compensation payable in any dispute
To exempt either party from liability for force majeure events

questionText: Which of the following is a key indicator of a successful foreign procurement outcome?
options: The contract was awarded to the supplier with the longest history
Goods delivered on time, within budget, and meeting the specified technical requirements
The procurement was completed without any supplier complaints
The procuring entity used the same foreign supplier as in previous years

questionText: What is the significance of "Incoterms" in determining insurance responsibility in a foreign procurement contract?
options: Incoterms set the premium rate for cargo insurance
Incoterms define at which point the risk of loss transfers, indicating which party should arrange insurance for each leg of the journey
Incoterms eliminate the need for cargo insurance in international trade
Incoterms require both buyer and seller to independently insure the goods

questionText: Which of the following is a key requirement for a valid international procurement contract?
options: Approval from the United Nations before the contract takes effect
Offer, acceptance, consideration, and compliance with applicable laws of the governing jurisdiction
Submission to the Public Procurement Agency in the buyer's country
Registration with the international chamber of commerce

questionText: What is the key purpose of conducting a "supplier market survey" before issuing an international tender?
options: To identify the winning bidder before the tender is published
To understand available supply options, realistic pricing, and technical standards in the international market
To determine which suppliers should be excluded from the bidding process
To set the procurement budget based on the most expensive available option

questionText: Which of the following is a key risk in foreign procurement related to intellectual property?
options: Foreign suppliers charging higher prices than domestic suppliers
The risk of procuring counterfeit or patent-infringing products, exposing the buyer to legal liability
Foreign suppliers shipping goods to the wrong destination
Delays in obtaining import permits from the customs authority

questionText: What is the purpose of "liquidated damages" in a foreign procurement contract?
options: To compensate the supplier for losses due to currency fluctuation
To pre-agree the financial penalty the supplier will pay for delays or non-performance, avoiding lengthy dispute processes
To cover the cost of customs duties on late-arriving goods
To guarantee payment to the seller in case of buyer insolvency

questionText: Which of the following best describes "duty-free" importation in the context of government procurement?
options: The government pays customs duties on behalf of foreign suppliers
Certain government imports are exempted from customs duties under applicable laws or international agreements
All foreign procurement is automatically exempt from duties
Foreign suppliers are responsible for paying duties on goods imported for government use

questionText: What is the key advantage of using electronic procurement platforms in international competitive bidding?
options: They eliminate the need for technical specifications in tender documents
They improve transparency, reduce administrative costs, and broaden supplier participation
They automatically select the winning bidder based on price
They replace all documentation requirements in international procurement

questionText: Which of the following is a key element of a robust foreign supplier qualification process?
options: Selecting suppliers based on the number of years they have been in operation
Assessing financial capacity, technical experience, references, quality management systems, and compliance status
Limiting qualification to suppliers that have previously worked with the Ethiopian government
Requiring suppliers to establish a local office before submitting a bid

questionText: What is the significance of "Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600)" in foreign procurement?
options: It sets import tariff rates for goods traded between member countries
It provides the internationally accepted rules governing letters of credit, adopted by banks worldwide
It establishes the Incoterms used in international supply contracts
It regulates customs clearance procedures in developing countries

questionText: What is the primary challenge of managing foreign procurement contracts over a long period?
options: Excessive competition from new suppliers entering the market
Exchange rate volatility, geopolitical risks, supply chain disruptions, and evolving technical standards
Over-documentation requirements from the buyer's procurement authority
Difficulty in finding sufficient international suppliers for common goods

questionText: Which of the following is a key responsibility of a procurement officer managing a foreign procurement contract?
options: Personally traveling to the supplier's country to oversee production
Monitoring contract milestones, managing documentation, coordinating with customs, and ensuring timely delivery and payment
Negotiating a new price after goods are shipped
Selecting the freight forwarder without reference to the contract terms

questionText: What is the purpose of a "certificate of free sale" in international trade?
options: To confirm that the buyer has paid for the goods in full
To certify that the goods are legally sold and approved for export in the country of origin
To authorize the buyer to sell the goods in the domestic market
To confirm that the goods are exempt from import duties

questionText: Which of the following is a key factor in assessing the "total landed cost" of foreign procurement?
options: Only the FOB price quoted by the seller
All costs including purchase price, freight, insurance, customs duties, and inland transportation to the final destination
Only the CIF price plus import duties
The seller's profit margin on the transaction

questionText: What is the purpose of "benchmarking" in the context of foreign procurement?
options: To set a minimum price for all foreign tenders
To compare procurement outcomes, costs, and processes against industry standards or best-in-class organizations to identify improvement opportunities
To restrict procurement to suppliers who meet predefined price benchmarks
To award contracts to the supplier closest to the benchmark price

questionText: Which of the following is a key consideration when drafting a dispute resolution clause for a foreign procurement contract?
options: Specifying that all disputes must be resolved in the buyer's country courts regardless of the supplier's preference
Choosing a neutral and internationally recognized arbitration forum, applicable law, and language to ensure enforceability
Limiting dispute resolution to informal negotiations without formal procedures
Excluding all financial disputes from the scope of the clause

questionText: What is the significance of "sanctions screening" in foreign procurement?
options: To identify foreign suppliers with the lowest prices
To check whether potential suppliers are subject to international sanctions, which would prohibit the buyer from entering contracts with them
To verify that goods comply with international quality standards
To assess the environmental impact of the supplier's manufacturing process

questionText: Which of the following is a key benefit of engaging a local agent in foreign procurement?
options: The local agent automatically takes legal responsibility for the foreign supplier
A local agent can assist with customs clearance, local regulations, language, and logistics coordination
The local agent guarantees the quality of goods supplied by the foreign manufacturer
Using a local agent eliminates the need for a letter of credit

questionText: What is the primary purpose of "commodity price risk management" in foreign procurement?
options: To ensure that all contracts are awarded at the lowest available market price
To protect the buyer from unexpected increases in commodity prices through hedging or price adjustment mechanisms in contracts
To set fixed prices for all goods regardless of market conditions
To eliminate the need for competitive bidding when commodity prices are stable

questionText: Which of the following is the most critical success factor in foreign procurement management?
options: Ensuring all contracts are awarded to suppliers from friendly countries
A combination of thorough planning, rigorous supplier selection, robust contract management, and proactive risk mitigation
Completing procurement within the shortest possible time regardless of compliance
Using only spot purchasing to take advantage of favorable market conditions
